status: Unofficial results from the Town of Oakville, all 57 tabulators reported. The Town Clerk declares the official results.

ward7.title: Who voted in Ward 7
ward7.headline: Ward 7 cast the fewest ballots in Oakville and turned out below the town rate

cards.l: ballots cast, lowest of the 7 wards (average 8,663)
estimated turnout vs 34.3% town-wide
Ward 7's share of Oakville electors vs share of ballots
growth in votes cast in Ward 7 races since 2022

points: Ward 7 has about 11.1% of Oakville's electors (19,718 on the September voters' list) but cast only 9.6% of the ballots. The turnout figure is an estimate, because the Town does not publish electors by ward and the list changes up to election day.
Votes in Ward 7 races grew 58% to 61% since 2022, faster than ballots town-wide (+48%). As North Oakville fills in, Ward 7 is catching up, but its turnout rate still trails the town.
If Ward 7 had voted at the town rate, about 910 more ballots would have been cast, more than twice the 376-vote margin in the Town & Regional race.
5.0% of Ward 7 ballots skipped the Town Councillor race and 5.1% skipped Town & Regional, close to the council average. Ward 7 voters who came out did vote down the ballot.

ward7.title: Ward 7 Town & Regional
ward7.headline: Nav Nanda re-elected with 40.5%. Bilal Kader second, 376 votes behind

cards.l: voted for a challenger (42.3% in 2022's two-way race)
vote margin (6.8 points), third-closest race in Oakville
effective candidates: in practice a three-way race
Bilal Kader's votes vs the 2022 runner-up (1,869 vs 1,454)

points: A majority voted against the incumbent. The challengers' share rose from 42.3% in 2022 to 59.5%, but it split four ways, and the incumbent held the seat with a plurality.
Nanda's base held and grew slightly: +261 votes (+13%). Votes in the race grew 61%, so almost all the new votes went to challengers.
Nanda's 40.5% is the lowest share of the five councillors re-elected. It is also below the 44.9% average winning share in Oakville's open council seats.
Bilal Kader's 33.7% is the highest share any challenger won against a sitting councillor in Oakville this year. His 1,869 votes beat the 2022 runner-up's total by 415 in a far more crowded field.
Vick Walia (833, 15.0%), Ajay Rosha (401, 7.2%) and Gaganpreet Darar (202, 3.6%) together took 1,436 votes, almost four times the margin.
The size of the gap: 189 voters switching from Nanda to Kader, or 377 more net votes for Kader, would have changed the result.

ward7.title: Ward 7 Town Councillor
ward7.headline: Scott Xie went from a 23% plurality to a 54.5% majority

cards.l: votes gained by Scott Xie since 2022 (820 to 3,027)
vote margin over Zulfi Malik (24.9 points)
effective candidates

points: In 2022, Xie won a nine-way race with 23.3% and a 133-vote margin. This time the field shrank to three and he took a clear majority. Four years in office turned a narrow plurality into a safe seat.
Zulfi Malik placed second with 29.6% in his first run for this seat, and Ali Hosny third with 15.9%.
Several 2022 candidates for this seat ran elsewhere this year: Ajay Rosha for Ward 7 Town & Regional, Amir Henry for Ward 1 Town Councillor, and Kashif Chaudry for Ward 4 Town & Regional.

ward7.title: Reading the two Ward 7 races together
ward7.headline: Same ballots, very different results for the two incumbents

cards.l: more votes for Xie than for Nanda on the same 5,846 ballots
incumbent share: Town Councillor vs Town & Regional

points: Both races were on every Ward 7 ballot, so turnout cannot explain the gap between them. Voters treated the two incumbents differently.
There was no general mood against incumbents in Ward 7. Xie strengthened his hold while Nanda weakened, which points to weakness specific to the Regional seat.
The Town reports only totals, not how individual ballots combined the two races. Any read on which Xie voters chose which Regional candidate is an inference, not a measurement.

ward7.title: School board races on Ward 7 ballots
ward7.headline: Ward 7 shares the most fragmented race in Oakville: HDSB Trustee, Wards 5 & 7

cards.l: winning share for Kim Tait, lowest of any race in Oakville
vote margin over Jake Zhu (4.0 points)
effective candidates, the highest in Oakville
of ballots skipped this race

points: An open seat with six candidates produced a four-way contest: Tait 27.5%, Zhu 23.6%, Lily Bharat 21.8% and Azra Ghumman 19.1%.
HCDSB Trustee for Wards 4 & 7 was acclaimed (Chris Saunders), so Catholic school supporters in Ward 7 had no trustee vote.
The Town does not split trustee results by ward, so Ward 7's own preference in this race cannot be separated from Ward 5's.

ward7.title: What decided Ward 7 Town & Regional
ward7.headline: A divided opposition, a ward that under-voted and an incumbent base that held
points: Split opposition: 59.5% voted for a challenger, but four challengers shared it. In 2022's two-way race, the single challenger took 42.3%.
Turnout: Ward 7 cast the fewest ballots in Oakville. About 910 ballots went uncast compared with the town rate, more than twice the margin.
Incumbent floor: Nanda's 2,245 votes were 261 more than in 2022. His base turned out even as his share fell.

Challenger strength: Bilal Kader's 33.7% was the best challenger result against any sitting councillor in Oakville this year, which makes Ward 7 Town & Regional one of the most competitive seats going into 2030.
What to watch for 2030: the number of challengers, Ward 7 turnout as new neighbourhoods fill in, and whether the anti-incumbent vote consolidates behind one candidate.

overview.title: Turnout
overview.headline: One in three electors voted, and ballots rose by nearly half since 2022

cards.l: turnout: 60,638 of 176,984 eligible electors
more ballots than 2022 (41,021)
voted early: 14,787 advance ballots (26.4% in 2022)
election-day ballots: 45,851 vs 30,209 in 2022

points: Two in three eligible electors did not vote. The new mayor's 21,866 votes equal 12.4% of eligible electors.
Advance voting grew 37%, yet its share of all ballots fell from 26.4% to 24.4%. Election-day voting grew faster, a sign of late deciders drawn out by an open-feeling mayoral race.
Turnout beat this app's pre-election projection of 46,000 to 56,000 ballots. The election-day surge was the part the projection missed.
Ward 4 cast the most ballots (12,400) and Ward 7 the fewest (5,846). The Town does not publish electors by ward, so turnout by ward cannot be calculated exactly from its results.

overview.title: Mayor
overview.headline: Jeff Knoll elected with 36.3%. Rob Burton, mayor since 2006, finishes third

cards.l: vote margin over Sean O'Meara (13.8 points)
voted for someone other than the incumbent
Rob Burton's votes vs 2022 (19,949 to 12,254)
effective candidates

points: A clear change vote: four in five voters chose someone other than the incumbent while turnout rose almost 48%.

Knoll won a plurality, not a majority (63.7% voted for another candidate). That is normal in a five-way race, and vote splitting did not decide the winner: Knoll finished 8,299 votes ahead of second place.
Both councillors who gave up their Town & Regional seats to run, Knoll (Ward 5) and O'Meara (Ward 1), finished first and second. Their ward-level profile carried them town-wide.
Julia Hanna fell from 47.1% in the 2022 two-way race to 17.7%. In a crowded field the 2022 result was not a guide.
The Town reports the mayoral result town-wide only, so there is no ward-by-ward breakdown.

overview.title: Council
overview.headline: Every councillor who sought re-election to council won. Six of 15 council members are new

cards.l: councillors re-elected in contested races
council members new to council
average winning share: incumbent seats vs open seats
seats acclaimed (Ward 1, 3 and 6 Town & Regional; no vote held)

points: Voters replaced the mayor but kept every councillor who sought re-election in a contested race: Chisholm (Ward 2), Longo (Ward 4), Lishchyna (Ward 6), Xie and Nanda (Ward 7).

New to council: Alexandra Caldwell (Ward 1 Town), Morgan Elliott (Ward 3 Town), Audrey Wubbenhorst (Ward 5 Town), Stacey Saunders (Ward 2 Town & Regional), Roger Lapworth (Ward 4 Town & Regional) and Mackenzie Grant (Ward 5 Town & Regional).
Jeff Knoll moves from Ward 5 to the mayor's chair, and Jonathan McNeice from Ward 1 Town to Ward 1 Town & Regional (acclaimed).
Incumbent margins varied widely. Longo held at 80.4% (79.6% in 2022). Lishchyna fell 20 points to 65.1%, and Nanda fell 17 points to 40.5%.
Open seats drew bigger, more divided fields. Ward 5 Town had six candidates and was decided by 202 votes.

overview.title: Closest races
overview.headline: Ward 5 Town, HDSB Wards 5 & 7 and Ward 7 Town & Regional were the tightest contests
points: The three closest races all involved Ward 5 or Ward 7, and each had five or six candidates.

Effective candidates measures how divided a race was: 1.0 means one candidate took every vote, and 4.0 means a vote split evenly four ways. The most divided races were HDSB Wards 5 & 7 (4.6), Ward 5 Town (4.5) and Ward 4 Town & Regional (4.3).

overview.title: School boards
overview.headline: Many voters skip trustee races, and two thirds of the trustee seats were open

cards.l: of ballots left blank in trustee races (0.7% for mayor)
trustees re-elected in contested races (Baxter, Karabela)

points: HDSB Wards 1 & 2 had the highest skip rate in Oakville: 14.8% of eligible ballots left that race blank.
Open trustee seats produced new trustees in HDSB Wards 3 & 6 (Mayville), Ward 4 (Davidov), Wards 5 & 7 (Tait) and HCDSB Wards 1, 2 & 3 (Jelic).
Catholic board races draw far fewer ballots because only Catholic school supporters vote in them: 5,018 ballots in Wards 1, 2 & 3 and 4,379 in Wards 5 & 6.
